system.summary: Index numbers select the number alphabet for the run that follows (62: table 1, a-i = 37..29, k-z = 14..28; 13: table 2, a-i = 38..46, n 61, o 60, r 57, s 56, u 54), with three-digit code numbers for names; the same family as targets/zobel1629, a different key.
system.sibling_key: targets/zobel1629 (Johan Zobel, Paris 1629): same index-switching family, different numbers. Not used to read these letters.
system.notes: distinct_symbols = letter values in the decoder's tables (24 in table 1, 14 in table 2), not signs seen. nomenclator.entries 0 is a placeholder: no code is solved. unread_groups = distinct code numbers in the two transcriptions (9 Vienna, 7 Glückstadt; 165 not counted). homophones: none in key v1; a second value for o (28) is suspected in the Glückstadt letter, not applied. A later key state (v2, key_history/) reads 64, 12, 10 as index numbers from a gloss and adds a third table; not used. Documents 3-4 (PR #545): key v3 (dudout/key.tsv): index 62/63/64 table 1, 13/12/11 table 2, 10/9/8 table 3; table 3 the mirror of table 1 with g 33, e 35, r 39 from the 1644 gloss; 251 a null; code 301 = the Archbishop of Bremen (marginal decipherment, image 425), so nomenclator.entries is 1; unread_groups not updated for 560 and 756 (see outcome.codes_open).

solution.what: Catalogue 2543 (sweep of 11 Nov 2026): unit 260651 images 37-38 viewed at full size; number cipher inside German clear text; no decipherment on or beside the leaves.

While transcribing the Vienna letter (b106), runs after 62 gave 'einige reale dienste' with a rule alphabet (a-i 37 down to 29, k-z 14 up to 28); runs after 13 gave 'sache', 'Fridericus' with a second table (a-i 38 up). Key found before the freeze (declared). Transcription frozen 04:11:09 UTC, md5 953fd409.
Vienna decoded once: 33 units, 17 S, 15 E (13 codes, 2 declared), 1 N: strict 17/33 = 51.52%; letter words only 17/20 = 85.00%. Below 65%: read in part.
Vienna: 5,000 shuffled keys, German 4-gram: 0 reach the true score (true -2.4750; best -3.4441 at seed 20261112; -3.4529 at seed 7, added 13 Nov). Short text.

b110: unit 260651 images 20-110 screened for more Pentz-family cipher: none fresh; a code 165 on image 38 left, line 1, missed by the frozen transcription: with it counted, 17/34 = 50.00%. Key v2 made from a gloss on Günther's letter (image 48); not applied here.

b157: Pentz's Glückstadt relations (unit 274999) image 2, a whole page of figures 14-37 with codes; key v1 table 1 applied unchanged (reader not blind: had tried it on line 1 before the freeze; frozen 13:30:55 UTC, md5 1e70795f). Decoded once: 68 units, 25 S, 31 E, 12 N: strict 25/68 = 36.76%. German: Hamburg, admiral, Norway, provisions, constables, fortress.
Glückstadt: 5,000 shuffled keys, German 4-gram (Simplicissimus): 0 reach the true score at both seeds (true -5.4767; best -6.7301 seed 20261112, -6.5759 seed 7).

Fridericia II p. 17 n. 1 cites Pentz and Hagen to Christian IV of 26 and 30 March 1636 (Bremen Nr. 29, 30 a) and paraphrases the talks: risk on content, no decipherment. Bricka and Fridericia II and IV searched: no print of either letter. Ny kgl. Saml. Fol. 616c not checked.

Folder rebuild (b190): both decodes reproduced byte for byte from the frozen files; every figure reproduced by scripts/build.py; the filed shuffle lines reproduced; the b157 'code units 11' corrected to 10 codes plus one fragment.

Integration check (PR #522): scripts/build.py re-run with python3 -I in the worktree reproduces every figure and leaves the files unchanged; own decoder written from the stated table rules (not the contributor's key file) gives the same letters as decryptions/vienna_1636-03-26.txt and as the Glückstadt unit list (288 letters). Images fetched from api.rigsarkivet.dk (48703328, 48703329, 52788770): Vienna lines 1-13, 15-18 (about 130 figures) and Glückstadt lines L01-L09 (131 figures) agree with the frozen transcriptions, except Vienna line 4 figure 8 (25, written like the 15 of reale: would give wolen) and the code 165 on image 38 left line 1 already declared missed. Strict recount by the README bar: Vienna 16/33 = 48.48% (berhuren is a transposed decode, a hole), Glückstadt 23/68 = 33.82% (doubtful-figure units nUr and Prouiant are holes); contributor's 17/33 and 25/68 kept as theirs. Own control with lang de-modern, same permutations: 0/1,000 for each letter. Pentz's key (letters 14-61, index 62 and 13) differs from Zobel's (letters 4-27, index 28-39): separate entries. Fridericia II p. 17 n. 1 checked on archive.org: cites joint Pentz-Hagen letters of 26 and 30 March in the Bremen series, no decipherment. Folder only, Status: in progress.

Documents 3-4 (Brice Dudout, PR #545): Unit 274999 (503 images) fetched with curl from api.rigsarkivet.dk; thumbnails 137-502 swept: number-cipher pages at images 321-323, 402-405, 408, 411, 412, 420, 425 (1644-45).

Documents 3-4 (Brice Dudout, PR #545): Image 321 carries a contemporary letter-by-letter decipherment over every figure: 41 figure-letter pairs; they fit pentz1636 tables 1-2 and index numbers, and give table 3 as a mirror of table 1 with g 33, e 35, r 39; 251 is a null. Pre-registration and measure frozen (21:35 CET), key v3 frozen (21:36).

Documents 3-4 (Brice Dudout, PR #545): Held-out (image 322 lines 2-11 + image 425, 286 figures, two identical passes, frozen 21:41) decoded once: coverage 99.6%, N = 0.760 against bar 0.75, best of 200 within-table permutations 0.145 (bar +0.30): PASS. Rigsarkivet images (ref 52788768 + image) 402 (all lines), 411 (7 lines), 420 (all lines), about 465 figures: agree except 420 L12 fig 4 (42, not 62) and L14 fig 4 (55, not 45), both inside holes. PR #558 (Malcolm McBratney): suspected homophone 28 = o in the Glueckstadt letter withdrawn: the three figures are 18 with a hooked 1 (b193 re-read, not blind). Image 2 (ref 52788770) looked at: the doubtful digit lacks the base stroke of this writer's 2 and matches the 1 of the adjacent 16. outcome.method_basis: The key was found from the ciphertext of the Vienna letter itself (rule alphabets fitted to word runs while transcribing, before the freeze), with no decipherment on or beside it; the clear German around the runs is context. The Glückstadt letter was then decoded with table 1 of that key unchanged. Neither text reaches the contributor's own 65% line. Documents 3-4 (1644, 1645): key v3 completed from the contemporary interlinear decipherment of the 1644 recto (key recovered based on adjacent plaintext), then applied to the unglossed verso and to the 1645 letter; the 1644 recto is read from that decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Integration check (13 Nov 2026), README read bar applied strictly, per document, never pooled: Vienna 16/33 = 48.48% (berhuren, a decode with u and h transposed that the reading corrects to BERUHREN, counted as a hole); Glückstadt 23/68 = 33.82% (units with a doubtful figure, nUr and Prouiant, counted as holes). The contributor's own first-pass figures (counts.txt, scripts/build.py): Vienna 17/33 = 51.52%, Glückstadt 25/68 = 36.76%. fraction_read is the Vienna figure, the catalogued document. Documents 3-4 (PR #545, dudout/), strict: Glückstadt 1644 26/28 = 92.9%, Glückstadt 1645 37/41 = 90.2% (contributor's 27/28 = 96.4% and 38/41 = 92.7%). Documents 5-9 (PR #545 second part, 1645, dudout/transcriptions/suite/), strict: 31 Mar 49/72 = 68.1%, 8 Apr 36/52 = 69.2%, 20 Apr Chancellor 14/16 = 87.5%, 20 Apr King 87/108 = 80.6%, image 420 25/36 = 69.4% (contributor's 91.7%, 86.5%, 100%, 93.5%, 86.1%).

texts.label: Christian Pentz to Christian IV, Vienna, 26 Mar / 5 Apr 1636
texts.summary: Pentz, sent to the Emperor in early 1636 to offer Christian IV's mediation and press Duke Frederik's claim to Bremen, writes in cipher that he has not yet touched on the [168] matter, that real services will be hard to obtain, and that he wishes 'Fridericus' were with the King again; the cipher words sit in clear German that is transcribed only around them.

reading_review.by: Claude (Anthropic), for Malcolm McBratney: a model reading, not a person, and not independent (sessions of the same project). The reviewer's own record should replace it.
reading_review.note: The cipher words fit their clear clauses (einige reale dienste swer zu erhalten sein; Fridericus wider bei euer Mt. were); thirteen codes unread; the clear text is only partly transcribed.

texts.note: read_share is the strict share at integration: 16 of 33 units (48.48%), berhuren counted as a hole. The contributor's first-pass figure is 17/33 = 51.52% (17/34 = 50.00% with the missed code 165).

texts.label: Christian Pentz (Glückstadt) to Christian IV, c.1629-30, image 2 recto
texts.summary: Pentz as governor of Glückstadt writes to the King about a letter to His Majesty, Hamburg, men come in, and asks for an admiral, timber from Norway, provisions, gunners and fireworkers for the fortress; probably early 1630, when the Elbe dispute with Hamburg led to a fleet under an admiral. Holes in most sentences.
texts.note: read_share is the strict share at integration: 23 of 68 units (33.82%), units with a doubtful figure counted as holes. The contributor's first-pass figure is 25/68 = 36.76%. 'Decoded, not read': most sentences have holes.

texts.label: Christian Pentz to Christian IV, Glückstadt, 29 Apr 1644
texts.summary: Pentz tells the King he can no longer harass the Swedes from Glückstadt as his raiding parties did, because the garrison was cut and the troops sent to Dithmarschen; at times only four men hold the ravelin before the Krempe gate, and the troops in Dithmarschen have done nothing against the enemy.

reading_review.by: Claude (Anthropic), for Brice Dudout: a model reading, not a person, and not independent (same session).
reading_review.note: Every cipher word sits in its clear clause; recto glossed by the contemporary decipherer and matched by the key; verso read by the frozen key alone, one word probable.

texts.note: read_share is the strict share at integration: 26 of 28 units (92.9%); holes {REVELLIN} (doubtful figures) and CREMPER (last figure 21 inside a table-2 run, a corrected decode). The recto is read from the contemporary interlinear decipherment, which the key matches; the verso was deciphered with key v3. The contributor's figure is 27/28 = 96.4% ('read').
